renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: correlation_heatmap
  title: Sample correlation
  description: |-
    Each cell is the correlation between the genome-wide bin counts of two libraries, with rows and columns clustered. It answers which libraries have the most similar signal.
    How to read: replicates of one target should form blocks of high correlation and correlate little with other targets or controls. A library that clusters with the wrong block can be a sample swap or a failed enrichment, so check the sample sheet and the fingerprint metrics.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is 1, since each library correlates perfectly with itself. The coefficient is Pearson or Spearman, whichever the run chose, and the clustering uses complete linkage.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/tools/plotCorrelation.html
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: sample

- component: table
  title: Sample correlation table
  description: |-
    Each row is a library with its correlation to every other library. It answers the exact value behind a cell of the heatmap.
    How to read: sort a column to find the library closest to or furthest from another.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: fingerprint_scatter
  title: Enrichment against divergence from uniform
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: the area under its cumulative-coverage curve on the horizontal axis and its synthetic Jensen-Shannon distance, the distance to a perfect input of the same depth, on the vertical axis, with one colour per library. It answers which libraries are enriched and how strongly.
    How to read: enriched targets sit far left, with a large distance. Inputs and failed enrichments sit near the maximum area with a distance close to zero. A point off the trend is a library whose curve is odd, so open the fingerprint in the MultiQC tab.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical line at 0.5 is the maximum value the area can take, as stated by the deepTools documentation. It is the area under the diagonal, which the documentation equates with a perfect input of infinite coverage.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/feature/plotFingerprint_QC_metrics.html
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Area under the fingerprint curve
    y_title: Jensen-Shannon distance to a uniform library
    reference_line: vertical
    reference_value: 0.5
    reference_label: Maximum area (uniform library)
  roles:
    x: auc
    y: synthetic_js_distance
    label: sample
    color: sample

- component: figure
  id: auc_ratio_bar
  title: Coverage concentration relative to a uniform library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library: the area under its fingerprint curve divided by the area expected for a perfectly uniform library of the same depth, coloured by the same ratio. It answers how concentrated each library's coverage is once depth is accounted for.
    How to read: lower means more focal enrichment. Inputs and failed enrichments sit near one and strong enrichments sit well below it. Compare targets with their inputs rather than reading one bar alone.
    Lines and annotations: a ratio of one means no enrichment, by this catalog's definition of the ratio. deepTools publishes no pass or fail cut-off for it.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/feature/plotFingerprint_QC_metrics.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: auc_ratio
    color: auc_ratio
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      auc_ratio: Area relative to a uniform library

- component: card
  id: auc_ratio_card
  title: Fingerprint area ratio
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average ratio of each library's fingerprint area to that of a uniform library, and the box shows the spread. It answers how enriched the libraries are overall.
    How to read: lower means more focal enrichment and one means none. A mix of targets and inputs gives a wide box, so filter to one kind of library.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/feature/plotFingerprint_QC_metrics.html
  column: auc_ratio
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: average, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: auc_ratio_extremes
  title: Strongest and weakest enrichment
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest area ratio, the most enriched library, and the second number is the highest, the least enriched. It answers how far apart the libraries are.
    How to read: a lowest ratio close to one means no library is enriched. deepTools publishes no cut-off, so judge each target against its own input.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/feature/plotFingerprint_QC_metrics.html
  column: auc_ratio
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: most enriched, with the least enriched

- component: card
  id: js_distance_card
  title: Distance to a uniform library
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average synthetic Jensen-Shannon distance, between each library and a perfect input of the same depth, and the bars show how libraries spread. It answers how far the coverage departs from uniform.
    How to read: the distance runs from 0 to 1 and higher means a bigger difference from a perfect input of the same depth, so enriched targets score high and inputs low.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/feature/plotFingerprint_QC_metrics.html
  column: synthetic_js_distance
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: average, with the spread across libraries

- component: card
  id: x_intercept_card
  title: Unsequenced fraction
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average x-intercept of the fingerprint curve, the point where the curve stops being zero, and the box shows the spread. It answers roughly how much of the genome received no reads.
    How to read: values near zero are ideal. High values come from low depth or from very strong enrichment that soaks up all the reads, so read it with the area ratio.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/feature/plotFingerprint_QC_metrics.html
  column: x_intercept
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: average, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Fingerprint metrics
  description: |-
    Each row is a library with its fingerprint quality metrics and their synthetic counterparts for a uniform library of the same depth. It answers the exact numbers behind the tiles of this tab.
    How to read: compare each metric with its synthetic value, since the expectation for a perfect input depends on sequencing depth.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/feature/plotFingerprint_QC_metrics.html

- component: advanced_viz
  id: metagene_profile
  title: Metagene signal profile
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: its mean signal in every bin across the plotted window. It answers where along genes or around an anchor the signal accumulates.
    How to read: an enriched target shows a peak at its expected position, such as the promoter for a promoter mark, and an input stays flat. A library with no peak did not enrich, and a peak in the wrong place points to a mislabelled library.
    Note: the window is a fixed number of bins, so the anchor labels of the run, such as the start and end of the scaled region, name the bins.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/tools/plotProfile.html
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Bin across the plotted window
    y_title: Mean signal
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: bin
    y: signal

- component: figure
  id: signal_line
  title: Mean signal across the plotted window
  description: |-
    Each line is a library: its mean signal in every bin of the window. It answers the same question as the profile above with a plain line chart you can zoom.
    How to read: compare the height and position of the peaks between libraries. Libraries of one target should overlap, and inputs should stay low.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/tools/plotProfile.html
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: bin
    y: signal
    color: sample
    labels:
      bin: Bin across the plotted window
      signal: Mean signal
      sample: Sample

- component: card
  id: signal_peak_card
  title: Peak signal
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest mean signal of any bin, and the second number is the median bin. It answers how far the peak rises above the typical level.
    How to read: a peak many times the median means a clear enrichment. A peak close to the median means a flat profile, as expected for an input.
  column: signal
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: highest bin, with the median bin

- component: card
  id: signal_spread_card
  title: Signal level
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median mean signal over the bins, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers what level the signal sits at away from its peaks.
    How to read: a long box means a strong gradient across the window. Units follow the normalisation of the run, so compare libraries of the same run only.
  column: signal
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: library_count_card
  title: Libraries profiled
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of libraries in the profile, and the second number is the count of bin rows. It answers how many libraries the window covers.
    How to read: the row count divided by the library count is the number of bins of the window.
  column: sample
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: libraries, with the rows behind them

- component: table
  title: Metagene signal table
  description: |-
    Each row is one bin of one library, with the anchor label where deepTools names one. It answers the exact signal behind the lines.
    How to read: filter to one library and sort by bin to follow its profile.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: pca_embedding
  title: Sample PCA
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: its score on the first principal components of the genome-wide bin counts. It answers which libraries have similar signal and which differ.
    How to read: replicates of one target should sit together, and controls should sit apart from enriched targets. A library that lands with the controls did not enrich, and an outlier within a group points to a batch or quality problem.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/tools/plotPCA.html
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    dim_1: pc1
    dim_2: pc2
    dim_3: pc3
    color: sample

- component: figure
  id: pca_scatter
  title: Sample PCA over genome-wide bin counts
  description: |-
    Each point is a library, placed by its scores on the first two principal components. It answers the same question as the interactive view above in a plain scatter.
    How to read: look for groups of replicates and for libraries that stray from their group. The share of variance behind each axis is in the table.
    Source: https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/tools/plotPCA.html
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: pc1
    y: pc2
    color: sample
    labels:
      pc1: PC1
      pc2: PC2
      sample: Sample

- component: table
  title: Principal component scores
  description: |-
    Each row is a library with its scores on the principal components and the share of variance the first two explain. It answers the exact coordinates and how much of the signal each axis carries.
    How to read: when the first components explain little variance, the groups in the scatter carry less weight.
